correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all exact quantifiers and normalizations from RESULT.md. The base U is continuous, compactly supported on [0,2/e], increasing with U(t)=1/log(e/t) on (0,1/e], and decreases linearly afterward; range [0,1/2]. On monotone arcs any continuous locally Lipschitz nondecreasing Phi gives an absolutely continuous composition of total variation 2 Phi(1/2), hence W1,1. For O(U), the |a|<=2r section has length 4r and m_U<=U(3r), producing kappa int_{r>ce^{-1/kappa}}dr/r<=C; away from the tip, a>2r has m_U<=2r G(a), G in L1 with near-zero bound C/[a log(e/a)^2], giving 2||G||1; large radii satisfy m_U<=||U||1/r and center support length at most 2r+2/e, yielding bounded kappa log(1/kappa). Chen et al Lemma 2.5 gives D(U)<infinity for the identical gamma=-1 normalization. If M=sup Phi(s)/s is finite, |Phi'|<=KM near zero and local Lipschitzness away from zero imply a global Lip constant L, hence D(Phi(U))<=L D(U) and O(Phi(U))<=2L O(U). If the envelope is unbounded, choose s_n downarrow0 with Phi(s_n)/s_n to infinity, x_s=e exp(-1/s), lambda_s=Phi(s)/2. Integration over x in (x_s,delta) and y in (-x,0) gives lambda_s D-level integral at least Phi(s)/4 log(delta/x_s). For 8x_s<r<r0 and |a|<r/4, negative and positive fixed subintervals each have length r/4 and force m_f>=Phi(s)/64; with kappa_s=Phi(s)/128 one gets at least Phi(s)/256 log(r0/(8x_s)). Both diverge along s_n and levels go to zero. For Phi(s)=s^alpha log(e/s)^(-beta), sPhi'/Phi=alpha+beta/log(e/s), and the exact bounded-envelope boundary is alpha>1 or alpha=1,beta>=0. Finite test samples are not needed.

value.rationale: The two weak endpoint functionals are meaningful competing derivative-free tests which fail as universal W1,1 membership criteria at p=1. Restricting to an explicitly established one-sided logarithmic cusp and admissible monotone outer profiles asks a natural sharper question: precisely which continuous W1,1 profiles pass both tests? The common if-and-only-if envelope is an infinite-dimensional membership classification, backed by independent upper and lower mechanisms, and its sharp loglog threshold at alpha=1 is a natural boundary. The result is more than a rephrasing of the known single U example or a negative subcritical counterexample. It neither claims a new universal characterization nor optimal constants.
